_meta.note: Miele IDENTIFIER LAYER (WM+DW). IMPORTANT: Miele BREAKS the distinct-product-number pattern used by Electrolux (PNC) and Whirlpool (12NC). Miele's authoritative consumer/support identity = MODEL designation (Modellkennung) + SERIAL (Fabrikationsnummer), where the serial's leading digits encode the PRODUCTION YEAR. The internal Material number (M.-Nr.) exists but is NOT the systematically-exposed join key. Generation (the F11 discriminator) resolves from MODEL RANGE + SERIAL YEAR, not a product number. Data-only; not wired into production.

identifierStructure.modelDesignation: Modellkennung, e.g. G 5000, G 7100, W1, WWD020, PWM 507 (commercial). The catalogue stores this.
identifierStructure.serial: Fabrikationsnummer (Fabr.-Nr.): 8- or 9-digit number after the slash on the type plate (official miele.de). Leading digits encode PRODUCTION YEAR (e.g. serial starting '98' => 1998).
identifierStructure.materialNumber: M.-Nr. / Material number: internal material/order number; NOT the consumer/support join key and NOT systematically recoverable model->M.-Nr at scale.
identifierStructure.type: Type/product-type code present on plate; used with model for service docs.
identifierStructure.authoritativeForConsumer: MODEL + SERIAL (Miele plate-finder asks for model designation + Fabrikationsnummer).

evidence.reference: Fabrikationsnummer = 8- or 9-digit number after the slash on the type plate
serial number + product type on the data tag
Miele WM serial leading digits encode year (starts '98' => 1998)

generationResolution.note: Generation resolves from MODEL RANGE first; the SERIAL YEAR disambiguates the G5xxx case.

dishwasher.note: G5xxx 4-digit: Discovery from year-of-manufacture 2019+ = NEW; older G5xxx = OLD. Resolve by SERIAL YEAR.
3-digit G### (e.g. G577, G767) = pre-2000s legacy; predates the modern 4-digit F11 split. Dominates our catalogue.

serialYearRule.method: leading 2 digits of Fabrikationsnummer ~ production year
serialYearRule.caveat: heuristic; Miele serial schemes vary - use production date from a service record where available

mappings.note: model range alone resolves generation; no serial needed.

evidence.reference: G 5xxx Discovery from 2019 onward = new; older G5xxx = old

catalogueFinding: Our Miele catalogue is model-names only (no M.-Nr), and dominated by LEGACY 3-digit G### DW models (G577/G767 etc.); the modern 4-digit G5000 Discovery / G7000 cohort that carries the F11 split is barely present (G7xxx=3, G5xxx-4digit few). So the flagship F11 conflict applies mostly to models under-represented in our catalogue.
